r: おうじょうぎわがわるい
lit: to be bad at the moment of one's ōjō, one's passing from this world

story.text: In Pure Land Buddhism, ōjō means leaving this world to be reborn in the Pure Land, and in everyday Japanese the word came to mean simply dying. Ōjōgiwa is the moment of death. To be 'bad at the moment of death' was to cling on instead of letting go; the phrase now describes anyone who will not accept that it is over.
story.source: Buddhist term 往生 (ōjō, rebirth in the Pure Land)

use.how: Predicate or noun form (往生際の悪さ): said of someone who keeps resisting after they have clearly lost or been caught. Also used wryly of oneself.

cue: Your friend clearly lost the bet, but instead of paying up keeps inventing reasons why it should not count and demands a rematch.

ctx.en: My little brother, who keeps shouting "One more time!" after losing, really can't accept defeat.

mean: to be carried away with joy
lit: to reach uchōten, the very top of the heavens

story.text: In Buddhist cosmology, uchōten is the highest of the heavens, the peak of all existence. To 'become uchōten' is to feel lifted to the very top of the heavens: so overjoyed that one forgets everything else. The word left its religious sense behind and now simply describes ecstatic, giddy happiness.

use.how: 有頂天になる / 有頂天だ: intense, giddy joy at good news, often with a hint that the person has lost their head and a fall may follow.

near.diff: 調子に乗る is behaving cocky or overdoing things; 有頂天になる is the inner state of being wildly happy.

mean: to catch someone off guard with the unexpected
lit: to strike at what lies outside someone's expectations

use.how: Often before a noun (意表を突く結末, 意表を突く質問) or as 人の意表を突く; the surprised person says 意表を突かれた.

near.diff: 裏をかく outwits an opponent by doing the opposite of what they planned for; 意表を突く simply surprises, with no opponent needed.

lit: numbness reaching its limit: legs gone numb from sitting and waiting so long

near.diff: 首を長くして待つ is eager waiting that goes on; 痺れを切らす is the moment patience runs out and one acts.

mean: having started, one must see it through

mean: to come to someone's rescue in a tight spot

mean: to throw away a chance or years of work

r: もとのさやにおさまる

lit: a drawn sword going back into its own scabbard

r: じゅうばこのすみをつつく
mean: to pick over the tiniest details
lit: to poke into the corners of a lacquered tiered food box for the last scraps

near.diff: 揚げ足を取る seizes on someone's slip of the tongue to attack them; 重箱の隅をつつく fusses over trivial details of anything.
